01

A useful review separates facts and interpretations

Start with the plan and what actually happened. Discuss strengths, gaps and contributing factors without blaming people. Agree on one specific change, who will try it and when you will check the result.

02

Cold-weather rucks

When conditions change, pace, footing and the kit you thought was fine may change with them.

  • Record surface, temperature and what you actually wore.
  • Note when you changed pace or route.
  • Write down equipment issues before you forget.
03

Urban night navigation

Reduced visibility makes familiar streets and surfaces feel different.

  • Plan a legal, well-lit route and safe crossings.
  • Carry a light and keep your group visible.
  • Compare planned and actual route choices afterward.
04

Team rucks and hard days

Shared work is useful when you can explain what helped and what held the group back.

  • Record how people handled changes in pace and load.
  • Identify moments where someone helped the group.
  • Change one thing for the next session.

Write your own after-action review

Record facts before interpretations. Agree on one improvement and a person responsible for following it up. This form creates a local text file; nothing is uploaded or published.
